title: CHARCOT-MARIE-TOOTH DISEASE, AXONAL, TYPE 2A1
alt_titles: CHARCOT-MARIE-TOOTH DISEASE, AXONAL, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT, TYPE 2A1
HEREDITARY MOTOR AND SENSORY NEUROPATHY IIA1

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A1 (CMT2A1) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the KIF1B gene (605995) on chromosome 1p36.

checks.claim: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A1 (CMT2A1) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the KIF1B gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We show that CMT2A patients contain a loss-of-function mutation in the motor domain of the KIF1B gene.
checks.explanation: The abstract links CMT2A to a KIF1B mutation, but it does not say the mutation is heterozygous.

checks.claim: The KIF1B gene is located on chromosome 1p36.
checks.evidence_quote: Confirmed mutation | KIF1B | CHR1: 10387567 | Y1087C
checks.explanation: The paper places KIF1B on chromosome 1. The 1p36 band is standard nomenclature for the gene's location.

paragraphs.text: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A1 is an autosomal dominant axonal (non-demyelinating) peripheral neuropathy marked by slowly progressive distal muscle weakness and atrophy, more severe in the lower limbs, with distal sensory loss and reduced or absent tendon reflexes. Nerve conduction velocities are normal or only mildly reduced. The axonal forms of CMT are grouped as CMT2. CMT2A is genetically heterogeneous: CMT2A1 is caused by mutation in KIF1B, and the more common CMT2A2 is caused by mutation in MFN2.

checks.claim: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A1 is inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern.
checks.evidence_quote: Confirmed mutation | KIF1B | CHR1: 10387567 | Y1087C | Heterozygote | Autosomal dominant
checks.explanation: Autosomal dominant inheritance is stated in Table 2. Patient 2 was also diagnosed with autosomal-dominant CMT2.

checks.claim: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A1 is an axonal (non-demyelinating) peripheral neuropathy.
checks.evidence_quote: Demyelinating CMT1 has a nerve conduction velocity <38 m/s, and axonal CMT2 has nerve conduction velocities >38 m/s.
checks.explanation: CMT2, which includes CMT2A1, is described as the axonal form of the disease.

checks.claim: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A1 is marked by slowly progressive distal muscle weakness and atrophy.
checks.evidence_quote: suffering from CMT2A symptoms including progressive muscle weakness and slight central nervous system defects
checks.explanation: The paper mentions progressive muscle weakness, but not that it is distal or slowly progressive, and it does not mention atrophy.

checks.claim: In Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A1, distal muscle weakness and atrophy are more severe in the lower limbs.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. The abstract does not say which limbs are more affected.

checks.claim: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A1 involves distal sensory loss.
checks.evidence_quote: Progressive, symmetric, length dependent, sensory motor, predominantly axonal polyneuropathy
checks.explanation: A length-dependent sensorimotor neuropathy is described in one patient, but distal sensory loss is not stated as a general feature of CMT2A1.

checks.claim: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A1 involves reduced or absent tendon reflexes.
checks.evidence_quote: tendon reflexes preserved in upper extremities but reduced or absent in lower extremities
checks.explanation: Reflexes are reduced or absent in the lower limbs.

checks.claim: In Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A1, nerve conduction velocities are normal or only mildly reduced.
checks.evidence_quote: CMT2 is defined as axonal hereditary neuropathy with a normal range of axon conduction speeds but exhibits severe axonal degeneration
checks.explanation: The paper describes normal conduction velocities (>38 m/s) but does not mention mildly reduced velocities.

checks.claim: The axonal forms of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease are grouped as CMT2.
checks.evidence_quote: CMT disease is divided into two main types on the basis of electrophysiological properties and neuropathology: CMT1 and CMT2. Demyelinating CMT1 has a nerve conduction velocity <38 m/s, and axonal CMT2 has nerve conduction velocities >38 m/s.
checks.explanation: The paper states that axonal CMT is classed as CMT2.

checks.claim: CMT2A is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: Although a KIF1B mutation in the same genomic interval was the first identified in a pedigree with CMT2A, only a few pedigrees with KIF1Bβ mutation for CMT2A1 have been reported until recently.
checks.explanation: Together with the MFN2 statement for CMT2A2, the paper describes two genes causing CMT2A.

checks.claim: CMT2A1 is caused by mutation in the KIF1B gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We show that CMT2A patients contain a loss-of-function mutation in the motor domain of the KIF1B gene.
checks.explanation: The paper links CMT2A to KIF1B, which matches the CMT2A1 designation.

checks.claim: CMT2A2 is caused by mutation in the MFN2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Mitofusin 2 (MFN2) mutations, which impair mitochondrial fusion and ER–mitochondria tethering, are responsible for the most common known axonal form of CMT2A2
checks.explanation: The paper states that MFN2 mutations cause CMT2A2.

checks.claim: CMT2A2 is more common than CMT2A1.
checks.evidence_quote: are responsible for the most common known axonal form of CMT2A2 (Züchner et al., 2004; Kijima et al., 2005; Lawson et al., 2005; Baloh et al., 2007). Although a KIF1B mutation in the same genomic interval was the first identified in a pedigree with CMT2A, only a few pedigrees
checks.explanation: The paper calls CMT2A2 the most common form and says only a few pedigrees with KIF1B mutations have been reported.

paragraphs.text: Ben Othmane et al. (1993) used linkage analysis in a large family with autosomal dominant axonal CMT to map the CMT2A locus to the distal short arm of chromosome 1 (1p35-p36).

checks.claim: Ben Othmane et al. (1993) performed linkage analysis in a large family with autosomal dominant axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease.
checks.evidence_quote: We have performed pedigree linkage analysis in six large autosomal dominant CMT2 families
checks.explanation: The study used six large families, not one large family. Three of them showed linkage.

checks.claim: Ben Othmane et al. (1993) mapped the CMT2A locus to the distal short arm of chromosome 1 (1p35-p36).
checks.evidence_quote: in the distal region of the short arm of chromosome 1
checks.explanation: The distal short arm of chromosome 1 is supported, but the abstract does not give the band 1p35-p36.

paragraphs.text: Saito et al. (1997) reported linkage of axonal CMT to the same region of chromosome 1p36 in a Japanese family.

checks.claim: Saito et al. (1997) reported linkage of axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease to chromosome 1p36 in a Japanese family.
checks.evidence_quote: we performed linkage analysis of two Japanese CMT2 families using markers flanking the CMT2A, CMT2B, and CMT2D loci. The highest cumulative multipoint lod score of 3.69 was obtained at D1S244.
checks.explanation: Linkage was reported in two Japanese families with a cumulative lod score, not in a single family. The locus is also given as 1p35-36.

paragraphs.text: Bissar-Tadmouri et al. (2004) found no KIF1B mutation in a large Turkish family with CMT2A linked to 1p36, which pointed to a second gene in the region. Zuchner et al. (2004) then found mutations in the MFN2 gene, which also maps to 1p36, in several families with CMT2A. CMT2A caused by MFN2 mutation is designated CMT2A2, and KIF1B mutations seem to be a rare cause of CMT2A.

checks.claim: Bissar-Tadmouri et al. (2004) found no KIF1B mutation in a large Turkish family with CMT2A linked to 1p36.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. This is a finding of a later paper (Bissar-Tadmouri et al., 2004) and is not in this abstract.

checks.claim: The absence of a KIF1B mutation in a large Turkish family with CMT2A linked to 1p36 pointed to a second CMT2A gene in the 1p36 region.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. This conclusion comes from a later paper and is not addressed in this abstract.

checks.claim: Zuchner et al. (2004) found mutations in the MFN2 gene in several families with CMT2A.
checks.evidence_quote: There are several pedigrees of CMT2A with MFN2 point mutations (Züchner et al., 2004; Kijima et al., 2005; Lawson et al., 2005; Baloh et al., 2007)
checks.explanation: The paper cites Züchner et al. (2004) for MFN2 mutations in CMT2A pedigrees.

checks.claim: The MFN2 gene maps to chromosome 1p36.
checks.evidence_quote: Although a KIF1B mutation in the same genomic interval was the first identified in a pedigree with CMT2A
checks.explanation: The paper implies that MFN2 lies in the same genomic interval as KIF1B but does not name 1p36.

checks.claim: CMT2A caused by MFN2 mutation is designated CMT2A2.
checks.evidence_quote: Mitofusin 2 (MFN2) mutations, which impair mitochondrial fusion and ER–mitochondria tethering, are responsible for the most common known axonal form of CMT2A2
checks.explanation: The paper designates MFN2-related CMT2A as CMT2A2.

checks.claim: KIF1B mutations seem to be a rare cause of CMT2A.
checks.evidence_quote: only a few pedigrees with KIF1Bβ mutation for CMT2A1 have been reported until recently
checks.explanation: The paper describes KIF1Bβ mutations as rare in CMT2A.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a Japanese family with CMT2A linked to 1p36, Zhao et al. (2001) found a heterozygous gln98-to-leu (Q98L) mutation in the KIF1B gene, which encodes a kinesin motor protein. The mutation lies in the conserved ATP-binding consensus motif of the motor domain, and the mutant protein had reduced motor activity. KIF1B-beta transports synaptic vesicle precursors along axons.

checks.claim: Zhao et al. (2001) studied affected members of a Japanese family with CMT2A linked to 1p36.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention a Japanese family or linkage to 1p36. These details may be in the full text, which was not supplied.

checks.claim: Zhao et al. (2001) found a heterozygous gln98-to-leu (Q98L) mutation in the KIF1B gene in affected members of a Japanese family with CMT2A.
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions only a loss-of-function mutation in the motor domain. It does not specify Q98L, zygosity or the family. These details may be in the full text, which was not supplied.

checks.claim: The KIF1B gene encodes a kinesin motor protein.
checks.evidence_quote: The kinesin superfamily motor protein KIF1B has been shown to transport mitochondria.
checks.explanation: The abstract calls KIF1B a kinesin superfamily motor protein.

checks.claim: The KIF1B Q98L mutation lies in the conserved ATP-binding consensus motif of the motor domain.
checks.evidence_quote: a loss-of-function mutation in the motor domain of the KIF1B gene
checks.explanation: The abstract places the mutation in the motor domain but does not mention the ATP-binding consensus motif or name Q98L.

checks.claim: The KIF1B Q98L mutant protein had reduced motor activity.
checks.evidence_quote: CMT2A patients contain a loss-of-function mutation in the motor domain of the KIF1B gene
checks.explanation: The abstract says the mutation is loss-of-function. It does not specifically report reduced motor activity or name Q98L.

checks.claim: KIF1B-beta transports synaptic vesicle precursors along axons.
checks.evidence_quote: The KIF1B heterozygotes have a defect in transporting synaptic vesicle precursors
checks.explanation: The abstract implies that KIF1B transports synaptic vesicle precursors, but it does not attribute this specifically to the beta isoform or mention transport along axons.

paragraphs.text: Zhao et al. (2001) found that homozygous Kif1b knockout mice died soon after birth, with defects in the nervous system. Heterozygous Kif1b +/- mice had defective transport of synaptic vesicle precursors and developed a progressive peripheral neuropathy resembling human CMT2A, with muscle weakness.

checks.claim: Zhao et al. (2001) found that homozygous Kif1b knockout mice died soon after birth.
checks.evidence_quote: KIF1B knockout mice die at birth from apnea due to nervous system defects.
checks.explanation: The abstract says the mice die at birth, which matches the claim.

checks.claim: Zhao et al. (2001) found that homozygous Kif1b knockout mice had defects in the nervous system.
checks.evidence_quote: KIF1B knockout mice die at birth from apnea due to nervous system defects.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that the knockout mice have nervous system defects.

checks.claim: Heterozygous Kif1b +/- mice had defective transport of synaptic vesicle precursors.
checks.evidence_quote: The KIF1B heterozygotes have a defect in transporting synaptic vesicle precursors
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Heterozygous Kif1b +/- mice developed a progressive peripheral neuropathy resembling human CMT2A.
checks.evidence_quote: suffer from progressive muscle weakness similar to human neuropathies
checks.explanation: The abstract compares the mice to human neuropathies in general, not to CMT2A specifically, and does not use the term peripheral neuropathy.

checks.claim: Heterozygous Kif1b +/- mice developed muscle weakness.
checks.evidence_quote: suffer from progressive muscle weakness similar to human neuropathies
checks.explanation: The abstract states that heterozygous mice have progressive muscle weakness.

clinical_synopsis.feature: Distal muscle weakness, lower limbs more affected
Normal or mildly reduced nerve conduction velocities

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a Japanese family with autosomal dominant axonal CMT (CMT2A1), Zhao et al. (2001) found a heterozygous gln98-to-leu (Q98L) mutation in the ATP-binding consensus motif of the KIF1B motor domain. The mutant motor protein had reduced motor activity.

checks.claim: Zhao et al. (2001) studied affected members of a Japanese family with autosomal dominant axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT2A1).
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention a Japanese family or autosomal dominant inheritance. These details may be in the full text, which was not supplied.

checks.claim: Zhao et al. (2001) found a heterozygous gln98-to-leu (Q98L) mutation in KIF1B in affected members of a Japanese family with CMT2A1.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not specify Q98L, heterozygosity or a Japanese family. These details may be in the full text, which was not supplied.

checks.claim: The KIF1B Q98L mutation lies in the ATP-binding consensus motif of the KIF1B motor domain.
checks.evidence_quote: a loss-of-function mutation in the motor domain of the KIF1B gene
checks.explanation: The abstract places the mutation in the motor domain but does not mention the ATP-binding consensus motif.

checks.claim: The KIF1B Q98L mutant motor protein had reduced motor activity.
checks.evidence_quote: CMT2A patients contain a loss-of-function mutation in the motor domain of the KIF1B gene
checks.explanation: The abstract calls the mutation loss-of-function but does not explicitly describe reduced motor activity.
